published_statement: As restated by Kabat & Nomura (READ): for a brane moving with velocity beta around the S^1 of radius R (circumference L = 2 pi R), GLP found G4 = G5/(gamma 2 pi R), i.e. M4 = (gamma 2 pi R)^{1/2} M5^{3/2}: the effective compactification radius seen on the brane is r = gamma R. The specific form the tree relies on -- 'eq. (39)', V_brane(r) = -(G m1 m2/(gamma L r)) coth(pi r/(gamma L)) with Yukawa range gamma L/(2 pi), and its comparison to the Eot-Wash null -- is as quoted by the o6o7 pass (/tmp/o6o7/final.py:7-12); it is NOT READ here, and the equation number (39) is unverified.
published_hypotheses: flat bulk M4 x S^1, single compact dimension of radius R (L = 2 pi R) (KN restatement, p.3)

brane a test hypersurface at fixed position on S^1 in its own frame, moving with constant velocity beta along S^1 relative to the frame singled out by the compactification ('boost-like isotropic', KN eq 9-13)
gravity propagates in the bulk (a 5D G5 / M5 exists) -- the potential is that of bulk gravity
Newtonian (weak-field, static-source) limit; sources at rest on the brane

KN eq (15) gives r = R cos(theta) for a tilted brane and eq (22) r = R for lightlike b^mu; the general statement is that the null bounds the brane-frame effective radius r. branelink.py:142/:97 use R_EOTWASH as KN's r, and KN eq 73 (read) 'take[s] this relation to hold in general, i.e. even for a brane that is tilt-like', so the tree's computations use r correctly; only the label at branelink.py:24-26, :160 is narrower than 'r' and broader than its boost-like derivation. rederivation.outcome: ALL 15 CHECKS PASS (exit 0, ~1 s). (1) Boosting the lattice vector (t,y)=(0,L) gives the brane-frame identification (-gamma beta L, gamma L), interval L^2 preserved -- KN eq (10) reproduced; a static brane-frame field is therefore periodic with period gamma L. (2) Independent preferred-frame route: the wave operator on f(y - beta t) is (1-beta^2) f'', so the steady field is harmonic in eta = gamma xi with period gamma L -- same result without using the brane-frame identification. (3) The image sum sum_n 1/(r^2+n^2 a^2) = pi coth(pi r/a)/(a r) checked numerically at 4 points to 1e-8; with the 4-space Gauss-law point potential -G5 m/(pi R^2) it gives exactly V = -(G5 m1 m2/(a r)) coth(pi r/a), the pass's quoted form at a = gamma L; far field G4 = G5/(gamma L), which with G = 1/(8 pi M^2) is KN eq (72) M4 = (gamma 2 pi R)^{1/2} M5^{3/2} -- GLP's result as KN restate it. (4) coth z = 1 + 2 sum e^{-2kz}: leading deviation alpha = 2, lambda = gamma L/(2 pi) = gamma R = r. (5) 2 pi x 38.6 um = 242.531 um. (6) Under the tree's GW170817 seat, gamma L - L <= 1.698e-19 m. (7) Tilt-like r = R cos(theta) <= R.

lacked_data: GLP (2011) is a kinematic result about flat M4 x S^1 -- the effective size seen by static brane sources is gamma L -- and needs no measured input; it is re-derived here twice (brane-frame identification, and preferred-frame steady field) and agrees with Kabat & Nomura's restatement. Data that came later: (a) the Eot-Wash 2020 limit (38.6 um at |alpha|=1, ~30 um for one extra dimension per snippet), which changes the NUMBER the tree attaches to r, not the claim; (b) GW170817 (2017), which GLP could not have had: for bulk gravity with boost-like motion it forces gamma - 1 <= 7e-16 (GKLP eq 38-39, READ), so the magnification gamma that GLP made observable is, on today's data, bounded to one part in 1.4e15 -- 'small extra dimensions are detectable if the brane is moving sufficiently fast' is closed by later data in the bulk-graviton branch, while the formula stands. This is evidence FOR M's hypothesis in the weak sense that later data removed the result's practical content, and AGAINST it in the strong sense: nothing GLP computed is wrong or incomplete on any datum found here.
grade_evidence: The mathematical claim -- a static brane-frame potential has period gamma L, so the Yukawa range is gamma L/(2 pi) = gamma R and a short-range null bounds the product -- is re-derived by two independent routes (15/15 checks pass) and matches GLP as restated by Kabat & Nomura eq (10), (72), fn 8 (READ). It is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree states it unconditionally (branelink.py:24-26, :160; LEDGER.md:93) while it holds only (i) if gravity propagates in the bulk -- a branch branelink.py:40-53 itself keeps open -- and (ii) as 'gamma L' only for boost-like motion (the general bounded quantity is KN's r: R cos(theta) tilt-like, R lightlike). Two further items are recorded, not graded: the datum 38.6 um is (per unread abstract summary) the |alpha|=1 limit, not the alpha = 2 or 8/3 appropriate to a circle, so the tree's 'maximal r' is likely ~29% too large; and 'eq. (39)' is unverified (GLP not read; GKLP's eq 39 is the GW170817 bound). Not WRONG: nothing is refuted. Not OPEN: the result is closed-form and checked here, and its content is READ via restatement, though GLP's own text is not.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restating the line as 'for bulk gravity and boost-like motion, the Eot-Wash null bounds r = gamma R' (the scope in which it is derived). To DATA-DEPENDENT on the number: reading Lee et al. 2020 (arXiv:2002.11761) and confirming that the one-extra-dimension limit is ~30 um rather than 38.6 um, which would move branelink's R_EOTWASH (and the Mbar5 and SME figures built on it) but not the qualitative claim. A reading of GLP 1103.2174 finding its eq (39) is not the coth potential would be a citation discrepancy, still not a refutation. A reading finding GLP's potential normalised differently (e.g. an extra pi) would be a convention discrepancy only; the form is fixed by the images.
